# Feature List — pipe-clamp (IDF-D7, Quick-Close Pipe Clamp)

Source: disclosure/pipe-clamp-disclosure.md (J. Ortega, 2026-10-16), Sketch 1 (sketches/sketch-1-assembly.png), Sketch 2 (sketches/sketch-2-section.png).
Example status: **working** = the inventor built or ran it (§7); **prophetic** = stated but not built.

## Elements

| ID | Feature | Disclosure span | Example status |
|----|---------|-----------------|----------------|
| F1 | Pipe clamp with a hinged cap that pivots on a hinge pin at one side of the base; a spring pushes the cap open when nothing holds it; closed by a locking pin through lugs at the free side; no tool and no loose bolt | §2 | working (§7) |
| F2 | Base plate: flat steel plate, 60 mm long, 40 mm wide, 8 mm thick | §3 "Base plate"; Sketch 1; Sketch 2 | working |
| F3 | Two mounting holes, 6 mm diameter, through the base plate, one at each end, 10 mm from the end on the centre line | §3 "Base plate"; Sketch 1; Sketch 2 | working |
| F4 | Saddle block on top of the base plate, 40 mm long (along the pipe), 40 mm wide, 20 mm high | §3 "Saddle block"; Sketch 1; Sketch 2 | working |
| F5 | Half-round groove, 26 mm diameter, along the top of the saddle block in the pipe direction (saddle groove) | §3 "Saddle block"; Sketch 2 | working |
| F6 | Saddle block and base plate are one machined part | §3 "Saddle block" | working |
| F7 | Hinge lug on one side of the saddle block, 10 mm wide, 12 mm high above the block top, with a 5 mm hole along the pipe direction | §3 "Hinge lug"; Sketch 1; Sketch 2 | working |
| F8 | Hinge pin: steel, 5 mm diameter, 44 mm long, through the hinge lug and the cap hinge lug; the cap pivots on it | §3 "Hinge pin"; Sketch 1; Sketch 2 | working |
| F9 | Cap: upper half of the clamp, block 40 mm long, 40 mm wide, 14 mm high | §3 "Cap"; Sketch 1; Sketch 2 | working |
| F10 | Half-round groove, 26 mm diameter, on the underside of the cap, matching the saddle groove (cap groove) | §3 "Cap"; Sketch 2 | working |
| F11 | Cap hinge lug on one side of the cap; cap latch lug on the other side of the cap | §3 "Cap", "Hinge pin" | working |
| F12 | Latch lug on the free side of the saddle block, with a 5 mm hole along the pipe direction, in line with the hole of the cap latch lug when the cap is closed | §3 "Latch lug"; Sketch 1; Sketch 2 | working |
| F13 | Locking pin: steel, 5 mm diameter, 44 mm long, round head of 10 mm diameter at one end; pushed through the latch lug and the cap latch lug to hold the cap closed | §3 "Locking pin"; Sketch 1; Sketch 2 | working |
| F14 | Compression spring: 8 mm coil diameter, 1 mm wire, 12 mm free length | §3 "Spring" | working |
| F15 | Spring pocket, 9 mm diameter, 6 mm deep, in the top of the saddle block beside the groove on the latch side; the spring sits in it | §3 "Spring"; Sketch 2 | working |
| F16 | With the locking pin out, the spring lifts the cap by about 6 mm, so the fitter can put the pipe in with one hand | §3 "Spring"; §4 steps 2, 6 | working |
| F17 | Pipe held by the clamp; tested: steel pipe, 25 mm outer diameter, 2 mm wall | §3 "Pipe"; §7; Sketch 1; Sketch 2 | working |

## Operation

| ID | Feature | Disclosure span | Example status |
|----|---------|-----------------|----------------|
| F18 | Use: screw the base plate to the wall with two screws through the mounting holes; with the locking pin out the spring holds the cap open; put the pipe in the saddle groove; press the cap down (spring compresses); push the locking pin through the latch lug and cap latch lug; to release, pull the locking pin and the spring lifts the cap | §4 steps 1–6 | working |
| F19 | Method of securing a pipe in a clamp, steps in this order: (1) place the pipe in the half-round groove of the saddle block; (2) pivot the cap about the hinge pin onto the pipe; (3) compress the spring with the cap; (4) push the locking pin through the latch lug and the cap latch lug; (5) release the cap, the locking pin holds the cap closed | §5 | working |

## Tests

| ID | Feature | Disclosure span | Example status |
|----|---------|-----------------|----------------|
| F23 | One steel clamp built; 25 mm steel pipe fitted on a wall board 40 times; each fit took one hand; no pin was dropped | §7 | working |
| F24 | A pull of 400 N along the pipe did not move the pipe | §7 | working |

## Background (not features)

- Problem: two-bolt wall-bracket pipe clamp; adding or removing a pipe needs both bolts removed and refitted while holding the pipe; two hands on a ladder, dropped bolts (§1).
- Prior art the inventor knows: standard two-bolt pipe clamps (DIN 3015); hinged hose clamps with a screw latch; no known clamp with a spring that opens the cap (§8).

## Questions for the attorney (implied or inconsistent; not entered as rows)

1. **Washer.** Sketch 2 labels a "washer" at the locking pin on the latch side. The disclosure text names no washer. Is it part of the invention (and where does it sit: under the pin head, or at the far end as a retainer)?
2. **Pocket vs. land width.** The saddle block is 40 mm wide and the groove 26 mm, which leaves about 7 mm of land on each side. The pocket is 9 mm in diameter and sits "beside the groove on the latch side" (§3). It does not fit in 7 mm. Does the pocket overlap the groove edge or extend into the latch lug, or is a dimension different?
3. **Base-plate orientation and mounting-hole access.** §3 puts the holes 10 mm from each end of the 60 mm plate. Sketch 2 (looking along the pipe) shows the 60 mm length across the pipe, so the holes would sit under the 10 mm lugs. Sketch 1 shows the holes clear of the block. Which way does the 60 mm length run, and how does a screwdriver reach the holes?
4. **Cap wall thickness.** The cap is 14 mm high with a 26 mm groove (13 mm deep), which leaves about 1 mm of material over the pipe. Is that correct?
5. **Hinge knuckles.** How do the hinge lug and the cap hinge lug share the 44 mm hinge pin along the 40 mm length (side by side, interleaved, one each end)? The same question applies to the latch lug and the cap latch lug. What are the dimensions of the cap lugs and the latch lug?
6. **Pin retention.** What keeps the hinge pin in place? What keeps the locking pin from sliding out when the cap is closed (friction from the spring load, a detent, the washer)?
7. **Pipe sizes.** Is the clamp to be claimed only for the tested 25 mm pipe in a 26 mm groove, or for other pipe and groove diameters? If other sizes, which?
8. **Figures.** Should there be (a) a figure of the cap open (spring extended, pipe being inserted) and (b) a flowchart of the §5 method? Neither is sketched. The method claims will probably need (b).
